title: The team skill matrix
blurb: Explain what a team skill matrix shows, where it is created and displayed, and how it guides training and task assignment.
question: A new delivery team wants a clear picture of who can do what, where the gaps are and what training is needed. Which organization technique should it use?

teach.h: What a team skill matrix is
teach.body: A team skill matrix is an organization practice technique that gives a clear overview of a team's capabilities: each person's strengths, the gaps and the areas for development. It helps the team assign the right people to tasks based on their expertise and spot training needs to close skill gaps. Plain English: a grid of people against skills, showing who is strong, who is learning and where nobody has the skill yet.

teach.caption: Nobody is able in Data yet: a gap to fill by training or recruitment. The skill levels shown are illustrative.

teach.body: By giving a structured view of the competencies the team has and those it needs, a skill matrix improves resource planning, encourages collaboration by drawing on complementary skills, and raises efficiency and the chance of project success. It also supports training plans and empowers team members, because it can show both current expertise and the skills people plan to build.

teach.h: Where it is created and shown
teach.body: The team skill matrix is a topic of the project kickoff workshop in initiating a project, where it is completed collaboratively to map each member's skills and identify gaps or overlaps. It is not imposed on the team by a manager. For delivery teams it should be displayed visually on the team dashboard, so everyone can see it and keep it current.

Larkspur Insurance is building a claims portal. In the project kickoff workshop, product owner Martha Quinn and her delivery team fill in their skill matrix together. It shows two strong developers but only one person able to run accessibility tests, and nobody yet able to analyse claims data. The team plans training for two members, agrees who pairs with whom, and pins the matrix to the team dashboard.

teach.text: The skill matrix shows SKILLS (who can do what), not DECISIONS (who decides what): that is the delegation matrix. It is completed COLLABORATIVELY in the project kickoff workshop and shown on the TEAM dashboard, not the project dashboard.

items: Overview of team capabilities: strengths, gaps and areas for development (7.4.1).
Helps assign the right people to tasks and identify training needs.
Shows current and planned future skills, supporting training plans (4.5).
Draws on complementary skills; improves resource planning.
Completed collaboratively in the project kickoff workshop to find gaps or overlaps.
For delivery teams, displayed on the team dashboard.

summary: You can now explain what a team skill matrix shows and how it guides training and task assignment. You can also say where it is created and displayed, and tell it apart from the delegation matrix.

A.q: What does a team skill matrix provide?
options: A view of who makes which decisions
An overview of team capabilities and gaps
A list of user stories for the iteration
A record of the project's quality checks
A.why: A skill matrix gives a clear overview of the team's capabilities, highlighting strengths, gaps and areas for development (7.4.1).

whyNot.0: Who makes which decisions is shown in the delegation matrix.
whyNot.2: Stories selected for the iteration form the team plan.
whyNot.3: Planned and completed quality activities are recorded in the quality register.

A.q: In which workshop is the team skill matrix completed?
A.why: The team skill matrix is a topic of the project kickoff workshop, completed collaboratively to map skills and find gaps or overlaps (Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: The team planning workshop refines the backlog and plans the next iteration.
whyNot.1: The project canvas workshop defines users, options, vision, benefits, risks, scope, costs and value.
whyNot.2: The team retrospective covers the good, the bad, the learning and team building.

A.q: For a delivery team, where should the skill matrix be displayed?
A.why: If a skill matrix is used for delivery teams, it should be displayed visually on the team dashboard (7.4.1).

whyNot.1: The project canvas holds the business justification, not team skills.
whyNot.2: The risk register records identified risks and their status.
whyNot.3: The release map is the project and stage plan.

B.q: A team lead wants to know where training is needed before the next release. Which technique should the team use?
B.why: A skill matrix highlights gaps and helps identify training needs to address skill deficiencies (7.4.1).

whyNot.0: Delegation poker defines decision-making within teams, not skills.
whyNot.2: Magic estimation sizes stories quickly in early planning.
whyNot.3: Story mapping breaks a product down into user stories.

B.q: A project manager fills in a skill matrix for the team without involving them and posts it on the project dashboard. Which statement is correct?
options: This is correct because the PM owns team resourcing
It should be on the project dashboard for the board
It should be completed collaboratively by the team
It should be completed by the agile coach instead
B.why: The team skill matrix is completed collaboratively in the project kickoff workshop and, for delivery teams, shown on the team dashboard (Table 13.8, 7.4.1).

whyNot.0: Filling it in alone misses the collaborative completion the book describes.
whyNot.1: For delivery teams it belongs on the team dashboard, not the project dashboard.
whyNot.3: The agile coach works at organization level; the team completes its own matrix.

B.q:
Which two statements about the team skill matrix are correct?
1. It can show both current and planned future skills.
2. It defines who has authority over each decision area.
3. It helps assign the right people to tasks.
4. It replaces the role descriptions.
B.why: The skill matrix shows current and planned future expertise (1) and helps assign the right people to tasks (3) (4.5, 7.4.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: decision authority is the delegation matrix.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: decisions belong to the delegation matrix, and role descriptions remain a separate product.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: role descriptions remain a management product in their own right.

C.q: Which practice does the team skill matrix belong to, and which workshop topic covers it?
options: Organization; team skill matrix in the kickoff
Quality; user story refinement in team planning
Plans; effort estimation in team planning
Progress; project highlights in progress review
C.why: The skill matrix is an organization practice technique (7.4.1) and a topic of the project kickoff workshop (Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: User story refinement clarifies acceptance criteria; it is not about skills.
whyNot.2: Effort estimation sizes stories; skills are not mapped there.
whyNot.3: Project highlights reviews dashboard metrics; it does not map skills.

C.q: A team's matrix shows that only one member can run security tests. What is the MOST useful response the matrix supports?
options: Remove security testing from the Definition of Done
Plan training so others build the skill
Raise an exception report to the project board
Ask the agile coach to run the security tests
C.why: A skill matrix identifies training needs to address skill deficiencies and supports training plans (7.4.1, 4.5).

whyNot.0: Lowering the DoD to suit a skill gap weakens quality rather than fixing the gap.
whyNot.2: An exception report is for a forecast breach of tolerance, not a single skill gap.
whyNot.3: The agile coach works at organization level and is not a team tester.

C.q: Which benefit of a skill matrix is described in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: It fixes the team's velocity for the stage
It sets the tolerances for each delivery team
It replaces the need for a team coach
It improves resource planning across the team
C.why: A structured view of available and required competencies improves resource planning, promotes collaboration and increases efficiency (7.4.1).

whyNot.0: Velocity is measured empirically from delivered work, not set by a skill matrix.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are set through governance, not by the skill matrix.
whyNot.2: The team coach role remains; the matrix is a tool the team uses.

reteach.title: Picking a pub quiz team
reteach.question: Before a quiz, you list who is good at sport, music, history and science. What does that list tell you, and what would you do next?

blocks.h: Who is strong, who is learning, where is the gap
blocks.body: Your list is a skill matrix. It shows who to put on each round, where two people overlap, and that nobody knows science. You might ask someone to brush up before next week. A delivery team does the same together in the project kickoff workshop, then keeps the matrix on its team dashboard.

blocks.text: A list of who is GOOD at what is a skill matrix. A list of who DECIDES what is a delegation matrix.

explain.body: An overview of capabilities, strengths, gaps and development areas, used to assign tasks and identify training needs.

test.q: Which two uses of a skill matrix are named in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Assigning tasks and identifying training needs
test.why: A skill matrix helps assign the right people to tasks and identify training needs (7.4.1).

whyNot.0: Tolerances and stage approval are governance decisions by the board.
whyNot.2: Velocity and release forecasts come from empirical progress data.
whyNot.3: Estimating and iteration planning happen in the team planning workshop.

explain.body: The team skill matrix topic of the project kickoff workshop maps each member's skills and identifies gaps or overlaps, collaboratively.

test.q: In the project kickoff workshop, the team skill matrix topic aims to identify what?
test.why: The topic maps each member's skills and identifies gaps or overlaps (Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: Risks to agile adoption are assessed with the Agilometer.
whyNot.2: Epics for the project backlog are created in starting up.
whyNot.3: Benefits and dis-benefits are analysed in the project canvas workshop.

explain.body: For delivery teams, the skill matrix is shown visually on the team dashboard, which the PM can pull information from.

test.q: On which artifact should a delivery team's skill matrix be visible?
test.why: For delivery teams the skill matrix should be displayed visually on the team dashboard (7.4.1).

whyNot.0: The project backlog holds epics and project-level DoR and DoD.
whyNot.1: The project dashboard shows release status, burn charts, risks and issues for the board.

explain.body: Building agile teams includes empowering them with training plans; the skill matrix visualizes current and planned future expertise.

test.q: Which consideration for building agile teams does the skill matrix MAINLY support?
test.why: To support training plans and empower team members, the team skill matrix visualizes current and planned skills (4.5).

whyNot.0: Value-based incentives concern motivating people to adopt agile values.
whyNot.1: Co-deciding values and accountabilities sets the boundaries of self-management.
whyNot.3: Project risks are shown on the project dashboard and in the risk register.
